stories.headline: Yankees' Aaron Judge returning to injured list with calf strain
stories.summary: Yankees slugger Aaron Judge is returning to the IL after suffering a right calf strain. He had played just seven games since returning from a lengthy absence for a broken rib.
stories.body:
Three-time AL MVP Aaron Judge will miss most or all of the rest of the regular season after the New York Yankees announced Friday they are placing him on the 10-day injured list because of a right calf strain.

New York said it will make the roster move Saturday. The placement could be backdated to Thursday, meaning it is possible Judge could return for New York's regular-season finale on Sept. 27.

Judge was pulled from Wednesday's loss to the Twins because of tightness in his lower right leg. An inning earlier, he had to run to the gap to track down a ball in the outfield, but he didn't show any sign of discomfort or slowness and later said he first felt tightness during the first inning.

Judge was 4-for-26 with 13 strikeouts and one extra-base hit in seven games since returning last week from a broken rib, which kept him out of the lineup for more than three months.

The Yankees, who have clinched at least a wild-card spot, trail the first-place Tampa Bay Rays by five games in the American League East entering Friday.

Judge is hitting .241 with 18 home runs and 41 RBIs in 66 games this season.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

stories.headline: Heat, Pelle Larsson agree to 4-year, $60M extension
stories.summary: The Heat and guard Pelle Larsson have reached agreement on a four-year, $60 million extension, his agents told ESPN's Shams Charania.
stories.body:
Miami Heat guard Pelle Larsson has agreed to a new four-year, $60 million contract extension, with a mutual option for the 2030-31 season, Austin Brown and Steven Heumann of CAA Sports told ESPN on Friday.

A second-round find in the 2024 draft, the 6-foot-5 guard avoids restricted free agency next summer and locks in a new deal with a mutual option that fully guarantees $60 million while allowing either side to opt in on 2030.

Larsson has become a foundation player for the Heat amid their offseason overhaul. He is set to have a major rotation role after averaging 11.4 points per game last season, up nearly seven points per game from his rookie season. Larsson also ranked fourth best in offensive efficiency in Miami, per ESPN Research, and fifth in minutes played.

Larsson started 54 of the 70 games he played last season and ranked in the top 10 in charges drawn last season, according to ESPN Research.

Miami's biggest offseason splash was the acquisition of Giannis Antetokounmpo in a trade that saw a package headlined by Tyler Herro and Jaime Jaquez Jr. going back to Milwaukee. The Heat also signed free agent Klay Thompson after he cleared waivers following a buyout agreement with the Dallas Mavericks.

Miami looks to return to the postseason after missing the playoffs last season for the first time in seven seasons.

stories.headline: FBI case against fake 49ers player adds more alleged victims
stories.summary: The FBI has identified 35 additional women who say they were defrauded by Daejon Love and Taylor Chan, bringing the total number of alleged victims in a case that included Love impersonating as a 49ers player to more than 60.
stories.body:
The FBI has identified 35 additional women who say they were defrauded by Daejon Love and Taylor Chan, the agency said Friday, bringing the total number of alleged victims in a case that included Love impersonating as a San Francisco 49ers player to more than 60.

Portland FBI Special Agent in Charge Doug Olson said the agency is working to verify that the 35 women are victims of Love and Chan.

"We were surprised how many people were victimized in such a short period of time and then to have that many more come forward," Olson said at a news conference. "It's a large volume for just a couple of subjects. Our concern is that this fraud could be replicated by other individuals that are out there victimizing other people in similar schemes."

Olson said the FBI believes there are more victims of Love and Chan who have yet to come forward. He encouraged anyone with information on the two men to contact the Portland FBI.

"We don't want anyone to be fearful of coming forward," Olson said, "certainly not for fear of embarrassment or anything like that, because we want to help them and we want to make sure that this doesn't happen to anybody else."

The FBI opened its investigation into Love and Chan on Sept. 30, 2024, over allegations that date from February 2022 to Aug. 24, 2026, the day the two men were arrested at the Boise, Idaho, airport. They have been charged with wire fraud and conspiracy to commit wire fraud.

According to the criminal complaint, Love and Chan stole more than $1.3 million from 26 known victims in at least four states. The complaint alleges that Love, 35, used social media and dating apps to build fake identities, including posing as a 49ers player and a wealthy Swiss real estate investor, and persuade women to send him money. It says Chan, 18, sometimes posed as his financial adviser and assisted Love in convincing the women that Love would invest their money with Chan.

"The victims in this case were targeted precisely because they were trusting, responsible people who they believed were building genuine relationships and legitimate financial futures," Olson said. "... They were deliberately manipulated through an extremely sophisticated scheme that blended fake personas, fabricated investment accounts, staged video calls and AI-reinforced false identities."

Olson said the fraud scheme was "bespoke" to each victim. Not every woman got the Niners player persona, but Olson said Love often relied on the professional athlete character to reinforce his income level.

"He was either a player, former player, a player on injured reserve, and whatever name he was using, he'd put enough stuff into the media searches so it was the first thing that came up on people's [Google] page," Olson said. "And it was not just the first thing that came up; it was like there were multiple things in there that would confirm whatever he was telling those folks.. ... The sports thing was always like a big part of it because you have to have some source of initial income to be an investor."

A Niners team source told ESPN that the club was not aware of Love and had not received any reports about him before it was contacted by the FBI in August.

"They were completely cooperative," Olson said of the 49ers. "They were very helpful in doing things that most people think are probably pretty simple, but it's not always that easy to confirm. Like, this person was, like, never an employee, never a player, not even ever in the NFL. They were able to help with a lot of that stuff."

stories.headline: What we learned: how Freo found its mojo; why Swans lost no admirers
stories.summary: Fremantle completed a stunning comeback as Sydney's remarkable finals run fell agonisingly short. Here are three things we learned from Friday night's preliminary final thriller.
stories.body:
Fremantle will play either Hawthorn or Brisbane in the 2026 AFL Grand Final after storming from behind to beat Sydney in a thrilling preliminary final at the SCG.

Trailing by 27 points late in the third quarter, the Dockers booted the last six goals of the game to record a famous 12.11 (83) to 10.11 (71) win and advance to the final game of the season for just the second time in club history.

Here are three things we learned from the game:

Frightening Fremantle just needed one finals win to help rediscover their mojo
With 60 seconds to play in the third quarter of Friday evening's preliminary final at the SCG, it appeared Fremantle were 35 minutes or so away from heading home the loser. Down by 27 points, the Dockers were showcasing the same stodgy ball movement that had led to that shock defeat on their home deck against the Hawks two weeks earlier. They were playing nervous, appeared unsure and uncertain, and looked anything but a team that had dominated the home-and-away season with 19 wins and just four losses.

But then up stepped Hayden Young.

After the three-quarter time siren had sounded, Young delivered an arrow from 50m out on the boundary to cut six points off the deficit and keep Fremantle's hope of a Grand Final berth alive. Two minutes into the final term it was livewire Shai Bolton's turn to execute in front of the sticks. Another difficult 40-60 chance converted and the Dockers were sensing their moment.

The frantic yet decisive few minutes either side of the final change were a sign of things to come down the stretch as Fremantle outworked and overpowered the Swans, kicking five final term goals and holding the home side to a solitary point in a lopsided last frame.

Without the assistance of Wharfie Time, the Dockers dominated the ball, contested possession, and territory -- a total contrast to what they'd dished up in the two hours prior. And in just eight days this club has gone from staring down the barrel of an embarrassing straight sets exit to sitting on the cusp of its first premiership.

Fremantle's pressure-releasing semifinal win over the Cats last weekend did far more than simply book a place in the last four, it provided belief to this playing group that it can perform and outplay the competition's best sides in September. Prior to the finals breakthrough against the Cats, this team had lost two straight finals at Optus Stadium; a third in succession would have been confidence shattering and likely led to questions over the future of Justin Longmuir.

The Dockers don't win this preliminary final without last week's gutsy triumph. It was the performance it needed to shake them out of their post-season funk. And while that may not have been on display for the bulk of the night against the Swans, it very much came to the fore late. That alone should have this club brimming with confidence ahead of next weekend's Grand Final.

Maybe Sydney did run out of emotional tickets ... but they shouldn't have lost any fans
With the Swans having just dumped five best 23 players in the aftermath of one of the biggest off-field scandals in recent memory, almost nobody was willing to give this club a chance of knocking off Brisbane in a qualifying final. The 53-point win will go down as one of the most unexpected in finals history, but the question on everyone's mind was whether Sydney could back it up in two weeks' time.

The answer to that question appeared to be an overwhelming 'yes' as Dean Cox's side brought the same level of intensity, effort, and dare to its preliminary final date with Fremantle. Just as they'd done against the Lions, Sydney had the minor premier rattled early and looked on course to be heading towards a third Grand Final in five years.

The lopsided final quarter will tell the story that the Swans ran out of emotional petrol tickets, but perhaps it was more the gulf in class at the SCG, which only prevailed late. Losing three best 10 players, plus captain Callum Mills to an ACL last week, was always going to leave a seismic hole that would prove incredibly difficult to fill, particularly in a final against the season's most dominant team.

Either way, these undermanned, perpetually written off Swans only enhanced their reputation this finals series. To be odds-on favourites to suffer a straight sets finals exit and yet fall agonisingly short of playing in another Grand Final shows the culture of this club and the spirit of this playing club, even if not everyone has embodied it in recent times.

There are many unknowns with Sydney, its list, and what 2027 might bring, but its fans should stick by them. Those that have represented the Bloods in finals have done so with class and deserve to be supported in the future.

Errol Gulden can win the Brownlow Medal in 2027
Errol Gulden won't win Monday evening's Brownlow Medal. That honour is almost certainly going to fall on Collingwood superstar Nick Daicos. But if there's a player that's catapulted themselves into such discussion for the 2027 award, it has to be the young Swan.

Gulden put on a clinic at the SCG on Friday evening with game-highs in disposals (36), kicks (25), metres gained (770), tackles (8), as well as five clearances and seven inside 50s. It was the second dominant final in succession for Gulden, who also starred in the win over Brisbane a fortnight ago.

But it hasn't just been Gulden's September form. There was no hotter player in the competition during the month leading into finals, with Gulden averaging videogame-like numbers through the final five rounds of the home-and-away season. ESPN's Brownlow Medal predictor awarded him 13.5 of a possible 15 Brownlow Medal votes in that time, while others believe he had five successive best on ground performances. Given his efforts across the two finals, you can certainly make the argument he's been the best player on the ground in Sydney's last seven games. That's an extraordinary feat.

Daicos will start favourite for the Brownlow Medal just about every year he laces them up, but he'll certainly have some stiff competition if Gulden carries this sort of form into 2027.

stories.headline: Source: Ex-U.S. defender Miazga set for NYCFC after Cincy exit
stories.summary: Former United States defender Matt Miazga is set to join New York City FC, a source confirmed to ESPN.
stories.body:
Former United States defender Matt Miazga is set to join New York City FC, a source confirmed to ESPN.

Talks between the two parties remain ongoing, with a deal expected to be signed soon, a source confirmed to ESPN.

The Athletic was first to report.

FC Cincinnati officially exercised a buyout option for Miazga earlier this week, taking into consideration roster rules. A source added that the decision was made purely from a squad compliance perspective.

"FC Cincinnati have waived defender Matt Miazga and utilized a buyout of a guaranteed contract," MLS said in a press release. "The 31-year-old center back will no longer occupy a spot on FCC's roster or count against their 2026 salary budget, retroactive to Sept. 2."

Miazga joined FC Cincinnati in 2022, recording two goals in 88 MLS regular season appearances. He earned the MLS Defender of the Year award in 2023 for his impressive season with Cincinnati, becoming the first player to clinch the honor with over 25% of the votes.

The defender has also made 22 appearances for the U.S. men's national team. He formed part of the squads that won the 2017 Concacaf Gold Cup and 2020 Concacaf Nations League.

stories.headline: How can erratic Chelsea find stability? For starters: Look to Brentford
stories.summary: Brentford's 3-0 thrashing of Chelsea served as a humbling reminder of what a well-run club can accomplish.
stories.body:
LONDON -- You could forgive Chelsea's new outright owners for casting an envious glance at Brentford on Friday evening.

Chelsea might have fresh clarity at the helm of the club and a much-admired manager, Xabi Alonso, in charge, but familiar issues remain. Brentford's 3-0 victory meant Chelsea's era of full Clearlake Capital control started with a humbling reminder of what a club with a settled identity looks like.

Chelsea remain in a state of flux, but it wasn't meant to be like this again. Their investment in the summer was meant to build a spine: midfielder Jordan Henderson and striker Danny Welbeck were there to bring solidity and experience. The signings were in Alonso's image. But this defeat was a carbon copy of last season's Chelsea: a limp effort from a side that teeters on the abyss of mid-match capitulation.

Chelsea's attack has been impressive this season, but without João Pedro up front, the previously deadly triumvirate of Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer missed their point person as striker Danny Welbeck was unable to click with the duo. Instead, what we saw from Chelsea was an organized performance for about 70 minutes, Henderson and Valentín Barco bringing some stability in front of the back four.

The match was even at that juncture, chances at a premium. But once the substitutions came and the legs tired, Brentford were ready to pounce. Muscle memory clicked in. They remained resolute at the back, patient in attack, completely comfortable in their own skin and with full clarity over who they are as a club both on and off the pitch.

All of Brentford's three goals will make ugly viewing for Chelsea. The hosts' first goal was from a corner -- a ball from Mikkel Damsgaard, a header back across the box from Jannik Schuster to Jaidon Anthony, who was unmarked at the far post to nod home. Their second was from a counterattack -- Chelsea were left empty at the back, Kevin Schade darted away and after his shot was well-saved, and Igor Thiago acrobatically converted the rebound home. And then came the final one, as Fábio Carvalho finished at the far post unmarked. Brentford coach Keith Andrews jumped into his assistants' arms and looked to the sky, as those in red and white chanted how they'd love to play Chelsea every week.

Brentford seems to be one of the happiest places on football's earth. They were unbeaten heading into Friday's match with a win and three draws. Frustrated sporting directors must look their way after another successful summer transfer window where much-admired midfielder Mamadou Sangare was brought over from Lens, and several other players were nurtured and improved here.

While Alonso was fielding pre-match questions on injuries and ownership changes, Andrews' pre-match news conference was more of a celebration: Schade and Vitaly Janelt had been called up by Jurgen Klopp to his 44-man Germany squad, and Nathan Collins' had made a £1,000 donation to Brentford supporters' group TW8 Casuals to help fund supporters' flags and general matchday displays.

"I love this place. I say to the players all the time that we don't realize how lucky we are," Andrews said. "We have a sign above the boot room that says exactly that; how lucky are we to be at an amazing place and be part of a special, special group."

As the Chelsea ownership look to the future, perhaps they should take a leaf out of Brentford's book. Since securing promotion to the Premier League in 2021, Brentford have barely missed a beat. Star players have been picked off by other teams, but still they trust in their wonderful recruitment to find ready-made replacements. No Bryan Mbeumo? No problem.

The same goes for their manager. There were doomsayers predicting Brentford would finally capitulate when Thomas Frank left last year and they promoted set piece coach Andrews to the top job. But the people inside Brentford are far cleverer than most in sport (and life, probably). As players nurtured and established in this corner of west London leave for Champions League football, the club just keeps on turning, integrating replacements already there within their ranks, or tempting an outstanding talent such as Sangare to the Gtech Community Stadium.

While the supporters waved their new flags, and whipped up this little part of London into a red-and-white fervor, they knew exactly what they were going to watch from their Brentford team. Sure, results are unpredictable and you can have the odd horror show. But fundamentally, this place is built on sturdy ground.

Chelsea remain unpredictable, still finding out exactly who they are and what they want to be under Alonso. He will come good, but if things continue to fluctuate at Stamford Bridge, keep Brentford in mind. Sometimes investing in what you have, with a clear identity, produces the goods.

stories.headline: Evgeni Malkin, in 21st season, will let health decide on future
stories.summary: Evgeni Malkin remains as passionate as ever about hockey as his 21st season with the Penguins begins. Whether it's his last, be it in Pittsburgh or anywhere else, only his body knows.
stories.body:
CRANBERRY TOWNSHIP, Pa. -- Evgeni Malkin remains as passionate as ever about hockey as his 21st season with the Pittsburgh Penguins begins.

Whether it's his last, be it in Pittsburgh or anywhere else, only his body knows. And right now, it's not telling the 40-year-old Russian star anything.

"I mean, it's a hard question," Malkin said Friday. "We see what's going on during the season, you know. And right now I won't say yes."

He also won't say no, though he has one clear metric that will play a massive role in whatever happens beyond this season.

"If I not feel hundred percent, I'm not playing," Malkin said, adding that if he is not helping the team to win, "I'm retired."

Malkin was able to turn the clock back a bit last season, posting 19 goals to go with 42 assists despite missing time with injuries. He averaged over a point per game for the first time since 2019-20 and seemed fueled by the desire to prove to Penguins general manager Kyle Dubas that he was still worth the investment.

Dubas played his cards close to the vest until after Pittsburgh's first-round playoff exit to Philadelphia. He praised Malkin's effort, and about a month later, negotiations that appeared a little tense outwardly resulted with Malkin signing a one-year deal to remain with the club where he has won three Stanley Cups, two scoring titles and an MVP during a career that will almost certainly end in the Hall of Fame.

The deal also extended the partnership between Malkin, captain Sidney Crosby and defenseman Kris Letang to 21 years and counting, the longest three teammates have ever played together in major North American professional sports history.

Malkin believes it's production, not nostalgia, that has kept them together.

"It's not we're just here because we win three Cups, you know," he said. "I hope we're here because we still play good."

The Penguins are banking on it. Pittsburgh largely kept together the roster that finished a surprising second behind Carolina in the Metropolitan Division, including re-signing forward Egor Chinakhov, a Russian who blossomed while playing alongside Malkin after being acquired in a trade with the Columbus Blue Jackets.

There are now four Russians on the team, allowing Malkin the chance to serve as a mentor in the same way former Penguins defenseman Sergei Gonchar did for him two decades ago.

"Any advice, any like, 'go to dinner,' you know, we just do it," Malkin said. "I'm the old guy here, and I just have the experience."

Malkin begins the season with 1,407 career points, 14 shy of surpassing Hall of Fame center Adam Oates to climb into the top 20 on the NHL's all-time list.

He's done it while serving as the emotional 'yin' to Crosby's more reserved 'yang.' If Malkin had ended up somewhere else, maybe he would had been the face of the franchise. He's long made peace with the trade-off.

If this is his final season, it's been a great ride. But he's not quite ready to head off into the sunset just yet.

"I think last year I showed my good games, and I am excited to be here," he said. "And again, like, I'm here to win."

stories.headline: Conor McGregor expected to fight in bare-knuckle once UFC deal expires
stories.summary: David Feldman, founder of the Bare Knuckle Fighting Championship (BKFC), told ESPN he would "bet everything" that Conor McGregor fights for the promotion once his UFC contract expires.
stories.body:
Bare Knuckle Fighting Championship (BKFC) founder David Feldman told ESPN he would "bet everything" that Conor McGregor fights for the promotion once his UFC contract expires.

McGregor returned to the Octagon in July following a five-year hiatus from the sport, losing to Max Holloway in the first round after sustaining a knee injury in the opening seconds of the fight.

The former two-weight world champion is also a partner in BKFC, which was founded by Feldman in 2018, and has one fight left on his UFC contract.

McGregor, 38, became a part owner of the bare-knuckle promotion in 2024 and is now expected to compete in the sport once his deal with the UFC expires.

"He has one fight left with UFC, when that fight is done I would bet everything that he will be fighting for BKFC," Feldman told ESPN.

"I'm definitely enthused by his enthusiasm. I didn't think we were going to get this out of him. I didn't think he was going to fall in love with the sport as much as he did.

"He's one of the biggest fans in BKFC, not just a partner. He says some really critical things that help us promote the fighters and do different things."

In the days after his short-lived return to UFC, McGregor confirmed he would have surgery on his ACL but hinted he could fight again in summer 2027.

Feldman said the Irishman is heavily involved with the business side of BKFC and expects his focus to shift to the sport fully once his UFC career is done.

"We listen to a lot of the different suggestions he has in building stars but he's been fantastic, he's jumping on board now since he started to recover from his injury," Feldman said.

"Obviously he's going to take another hiatus when he trains for his next UFC fight and then it's all BKFC."

BKFC will host its next event in Manchester, England, on Sept. 26, with Darren Till facing fellow former UFC star Yoel Romero.

stories.headline: Does the law back Enes Kanter Freedom's WNBA draft bid?
stories.summary: Enes Kanter Freedom declared himself a woman and said he's eligible for the WNBA draft. Legal experts point out strengths and flaws in his case.
stories.body:
The WNBA returned to action Thursday night after a three-week break. Congress welcomed the league back by demanding answers about eligibility and accountability.

In a Sept. 17 letter addressed to WNBA commissioner Cathy Engelbert, five members of the U.S. House of Representatives, including two representatives from Indiana, criticized the league for not prioritizing player and fan safety. Among the concerns was how the WNBA determines who is eligible to play.

"As a women's sports league, the WNBA must ensure the League remains exclusively for biological women," the letter said. "As Sophie Cunningham has commented, women should not have to face biological men playing in the WNBA. Opening eligibility to biological men would not only create an unfair advantage but would also risk player safety for the women playing in the WNBA."

Debate around who is eligible to play in the WNBA has raged since Cunningham told ESPN in a July 21 article that she supported restrictions on transgender girls and women in girls' and women's sports.

"I got a lot of negative feedback about me hating trans. And I'm like, 'I never once said that,'" the Fever guard said in the article. "I think that I am here to extend love. But I also think with that love is truth, being honest. And I want to protect young girls in a locker room or young girls in sport who shouldn't have to go against biological men."

Demonstrations supporting and criticizing Cunningham popped up at Fever games across the country in July and August. Former NBA player Enes Kanter Freedom stoked the flames by declaring for the WNBA draft in an Instagram post.

"If simply declaring who you are is all that's required, then I meet every single requirement necessary to compete in the WNBA," Kanter Freedom said, wearing an orange WNBA hoodie, in the Aug. 7 video.

The 6-foot-10 Kanter Freedom played 11 seasons in the NBA and last appeared for the Celtics on Feb. 8, 2022. Hours later, former fringe NBA player Royce White also declared for the draft.

Kanter Freedom sat in a baseline seat for an Aug. 23 game between the Chicago Sky and Indiana Fever wearing a black shirt that read, "Woman noun. adult human female." After scoring on an acrobatic layup in the third quarter, Natasha Cloud walked toward the baseline and yelled at him. Kanter Freedom stretched out his arms and stepped toward Cloud as she was surrounded by teammates and security.

Kanter Freedom was ejected from the game.

While most people in and around the WNBA don't believe Kanter Freedom and White are acting in good faith, the former NBA players have exposed potential WNBA legal vulnerabilities.

Kanter Freedom released the following statement to ESPN through a spokesperson at the America First Policy Institute: "Under the current WNBA rules, I am one of the most eligible players to be considered for the upcoming draft. I am not going to allow the league or the teams to conspire against me to deny me opportunities that their own collective bargaining agreement allows, nor am I going to allow the league or the arena to prevent freely exercising my First Amendment rights."

Matt Gaetz, White's attorney, did not respond to an interview request from ESPN.

Cunningham and the Fever return to the court Friday night for the first time since Aug. 28, when White sat courtside at Indiana's Gainbridge Fieldhouse wearing a blond wig. What could possibly be next?

ESPN spoke to five employment attorneys as well as league and union sources -- some speaking on the condition of anonymity -- seeking answers.

Who is eligible to play in the WNBA?

The 2026 CBA states that "only players who are women are eligible to play in the WNBA." Similar clauses have been in each of the league's six CBAs beginning with the first in 1999. The document does not elaborate on who the WNBA considers to be a woman or any process by which a transgender woman could become eligible. The WNBA is not alone. The National Women's Soccer League adopted a gender eligibility policy in 2021 but abandoned it in 2022. "Our policies are our practice, which is that every player who plays in this league has been determined to be eligible, and we're continuing to apply that on a consistent basis," NWSL commissioner Jessica Berman told reporters in August. The Professional Women's Hockey League also operates without a formal policy and there is no statement of eligibility in its CBA.

The policy landscape in elite women's sports has shifted significantly in the past half-decade. From 2015-21, the International Olympic Committee (IOC) allowed transgender women to compete in the women's category provided they suppressed their testosterone below a specific threshold for one year. The NCAA operated under a similar policy from 2010-22. Both organizations also had rules for transgender men and intersex athletes. The NCAA has since restricted women's sports in all three divisions to only those whose birth sex is female. The IOC went a step further, barring transgender and intersex women from women's competition. The U.S. Olympic and Paralympic Committee has pushed similar bans through the national governing bodies.

Is it legal for a business to require its employees to be a specific sex?

Almost never. But sometimes. Title VII of the Civil Rights Act of 1964 bars discrimination in employment on the basis of a number of traits, including sex. However, it allows for something called a bona fide occupational qualification. It's defined as a "limited exception for discrimination based on sex, religion, or national origin" if it is a necessary qualification for the business or the job. As an example, opening casting for the title character in "Erin Brockovich" only to women is fine.

So is the WNBA immune to claims of sex-based discrimination?

Not even close. The WNBA, which operates in multiple states, is subject to both state and federal anti-discrimination laws. Title VII states it is unlawful for an employer "to fail or refuse to hire or to discharge any individual ... because of such individual's race, color, religion, sex, or national origin." In 2020, the Supreme Court ruled in Bostock v. Clayton County, Georgia, that firing someone "merely for being gay or transgender" violated Title VII.

Members of WNBA teams are not just athletes, they are employees. The legality of a transgender athlete policy in American women's professional sports has never been litigated.

The WNBA could enact a policy that would bar anyone whose birth sex was not female from playing in the league. Alternatively, the WNBA could enact a policy that would establish a process by which a transgender or intersex woman could play in the league. If challenged, the league and/or the union would have a path in court to argue the policy should be permissible as a bona fide occupational qualification.

"What the WNBA would argue, I think, if they were presented with this issue, is, you know, the essence of our business is we are a women's sports league, so therefore we can restrict this," said Nathan J. Oleson, an employment lawyer and shareholder at Littler Mendelson. "They can use that sort of defense to argue we only want women who were assigned female at birth, or we want to define women to include transgender females and define where on the spectrum we determine that those people become women."

Does Title IX contain any direction for the league?

The Supreme Court ruled in 2026 that state laws barring transgender women and girls from school and collegiate sports did not violate Title IX. The 1972 law is often invoked as being synonymous with women's sports, but it bars sex-based discrimination in education, including extracurricular programs, funded by schools. Title IX required schools and colleges to fund girls' and women's sports or risk losing federal funding. The WNBA is a private business and not subject to Title IX because it's not an educational institution.

Has a transgender woman ever played in the WNBA?

No. Two nonbinary athletes have played for WNBA teams, but both of those athletes' birth sex was female.

What are the paths for a transgender woman to play in the WNBA, and how hard would it be to make the league?

It's a stretch to think that any up-and-coming American transgender girl or woman would be able to navigate all the obstacles in her way. For one, fewer than half the states allow transgender girls to compete in high school girls' sports. If a transgender girl played in one of the 21 states that still does allow it, then the door would be closed in college because the NCAA has banned transgender women from women's competition in all three divisions. Same for NAIA. It's worth noting that even when transgender girls and women could follow a tried-and-true path, none made it to the WNBA. Take away the coaching and competition benefits in high school and college, and the possibility goes from slim to virtually none.

In theory, a gifted, young trans athlete in the U.S. could find somewhere to play abroad until she's draft-eligible and then be drafted by a WNBA team. There is a 34-year-old transgender woman currently playing in the second-tier French league who could potentially be eligible for the WNBA, but given her age and that she's not a top-level player in the country's best league, she's not likely to get a look by the WNBA, which is considerably more competitive.

A transgender woman transitioning as an adult or after beginning an athletic career in men's sports could also seek entry into the league like Renée Richards did in women's tennis in the 1970s. But that has never happened in the league's 30-year history.

What has the WNBA said about Kanter Freedom and White's eligibility for the 2027 draft?

Following a meeting of the league's anti-hate task force on Aug. 12, the WNBA released a statement, implying that Kanter Freedom and White are not eligible to be drafted. "There are no immediate eligibility matters affecting the WNBA and we strongly denounce the bad-faith efforts to use these topics to demean or marginalize others," the statement read in part. The WNBA declined to clarify to ESPN how it came to that determination.

The 2026 CBA does not contain a clear answer. The CBA lays out the criteria for someone to be draft-eligible, but it focuses on age. A player competing in the United States must be turning 22 years old the year of the draft and have no remaining college eligibility or renounce that eligibility. Players are also eligible if they've graduated from college, or will within three months of the draft and have either exhausted their eligibility or renounced it. The same is true for players who did not attend college, as long as they are four years removed from high school.

International athletes playing abroad either at the amateur or professional levels are eligible if they will be 20 the year of the draft. If an international athlete plays in the NCAA, they are subject to the same criteria as American players playing collegiate basketball in the United States.

Kanter Freedom, who came to the United States from Turkey to play basketball when he was 17, was 20 in 2012. Royce White grew up in Minnesota. He graduated high school in 2009 and was in the 2013 collegiate class.

The CBA says that players are eligible for two WNBA drafts and three for late-matriculating international players. Athletes are eligible to be signed as free agents if they have previously been eligible for the WNBA draft. If White and Kanter Freedom had been eligible for a previous draft -- which seems implausible considering they never identified as women before -- they would now be eligible to be signed.

Can Kanter Freedom and White sue to try and play in the WNBA?

This is where things get interesting. To bring a Title VII claim, Kanter Freedom and White would need to file with the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (EEOC). The EEOC could investigate, and if it finds cause to believe discrimination occurred, the agency could sue the WNBA. The agency can also, however, opt not to investigate itself and issue a "right to sue" notice to the party alleging discrimination, clearing the way for a lawsuit. According to Oleson, a Title VII claim could be dismissed from court and sent to arbitration if there is a "clear and unmistakable" agreement to handle discrimination claims through arbitration in the CBA.

State employment laws also apply. If Kanter Freedom and White were to press the issue of their eligibility by bringing a state-level claim, and the players' union agreed with their position, but the league did not, Oleson says that would likely trigger arbitration under the Labor Management Relations Act (LMRA) to decide how "women" should be defined.

"There's a long line of case authority under federal labor law," Oleson said. "It says because we have such a strong interest in this country in allowing unions and employers to figure out their disputes based on the processes they've agreed to, that if there's a dispute about what 'woman' means under the [WNBA] CBA, that goes to arbitration. It doesn't go straight to the court system."

If, however, the WNBPA and the league both agreed that Kanter Freedom and White were ineligible under the current CBA, LMRA would not apply and a case could proceed to court.

Can teams just quietly agree to not draft or sign Kanter Freedom and White?

If they did, it would violate the CBA. The CBA bars teams from entering "into any contracts, combinations or conspiracies, express or implied, with the WNBA or any other WNBA Team, their employees or agents" to decide who should or should not be offered an opportunity in the WNBA. In other words, the league bars collusion. This is standard practice in professional sports, but there have been accusations of collusion. In the 1980s, for example, the MLBPA accused the owners of colluding to suppress free-agent salaries. The owners paid the union a $280 million settlement in 1990.

Collusion aside, each team could independently decide not to sign Kanter Freedom or White for a variety of reasons. There are players who are good enough to play in the WNBA right now who are not on rosters because of concerns about chemistry, commitment, work ethic or other reasons routinely cited by hiring managers choosing between job candidates. That does not immediately mean WNBA teams colluded to keep them out. Such an allegation would have to be proven, either in court or arbitration.

So what arguments could be made in court?

If Kanter Freedom and White decided to sue to try and force the WNBA to let them play, a relevant legal question would be their identities. When White announced that he would be eligible for the draft, he told Fox News Digital, "I'm transgender. I'm a woman. I identify as sometimes identifying as a woman for purpose of basketball, professional basketball, so I'll be declaring for the WNBA draft in 2027 as well."

In a lawsuit filed on Sept. 3 arguing the Chicago Sky violated his First Amendment rights when he was ejected from the Aug. 23 Sky game against the Fever, Kanter Freedom is referred to with he/him pronouns and the document says that Kanter Freedom "has self-identified as a player who is eligible to play in the WNBA." It does not identify him as a woman.

In general, the courts take identity at face value. In states that allow transgender girls to compete in girls' sports without legal or medical intervention, like Connecticut, it's not uncommon to require a level of identity authenticity, often proved through school records and how a student presents in school activities. Kanter Freedom and White saying they are transgender would likely be litigated, specifically questioning the authenticity of those claims.

"And then you know what would be discoverable? Any and all text messages, communications, emails, phone calls that they have had about this topic and about this stunt," said Susie Cirilli, an employment law expert at Spector Gadon Rosen Vinci P.C. who represents a number of transgender athletes.

Kanter Freedom and White would be deposed under oath. They could be asked to produce medical and psychological records corroborating their claims of being transgender women. Friends, family and agents could also be deposed.

"It would be my strong expectation that if a person claims to be transgender and alleged a legal claim and the defendant could establish that the plaintiff was not transgender, that would suffice to defeat the claim," said another lawyer, requesting anonymity, who has worked on transgender issues.

Kanter Freedom says he meets "every single requirement necessary to compete in the WNBA," but what about testosterone levels?

There is a robust anti-doping protocol outlined in the CBA. Players are randomly tested at intervals throughout the season for banned substances, including testosterone. There is no publicly available threshold for naturally occurring (endogenous) testosterone in the CBA. The league and union declined to answer questions from ESPN about the process should a player have higher than expected endogenous testosterone.

What policy could the WNBA enact if it did not want to include transgender and intersex women?

The WNBA could choose to enact a policy that defines "woman" as determined by birth sex, specifically requiring an SRY-gene test, which is already being used in some international competitions. An SRY-gene test is a proxy for identifying the presence of a Y chromosome. Transgender women have Y chromosomes because their birth sex is male. However, there are athletes with intersex variations who may also test positive for the SRY-gene.

Andrew Sinclair discovered the SRY-gene in 1990 and has pushed back against its use for this purpose. "Using SRY to establish biological sex is wrong because all it tells you is whether or not the gene is present," Sinclair wrote in The Conversation. "It does not tell you how SRY is functioning, whether a testis has formed, whether testosterone is produced and, if so, whether it can be used by the body."

For some, exclusion is the only legal path forward.

"In most cases, sex doesn't matter for the law, and in fact, taking it into account is what the law is trying to prevent," said Inez Feltscher Stepman, a legal analyst for the Independent Women's Law Center. "But in some cases, the law requires that you recognize sex."

What policy could the WNBA enact if it wanted to include transgender and intersex women?

Prior to 2020 when Idaho passed the first law that barred transgender girls and women from girls' and women's sports and kicked off a wave of similar legislative and policy changes, sports leagues and governing bodies allowed transgender women to compete in the women's category under specific conditions. The WNBA could choose to adopt a similar policy that requires testosterone suppression under a threshold for a specific duration.

Similarly, the WNBA could expound upon its definition of "woman" in a way that allows for some intersex women to be eligible.

Any such policy would likely be litigated.

"There's always been requirements to do a job, and so this is just the next thing that lawyers, and people in the league need to put their heads together on," Cirilli said. "But the result cannot be exclusion that violates federal law."

If the WNBA opts to codify its policy, how does that process work?

Eligibility to play in the league is collectively bargained, so any change would likely need to be as well. Following the anti-hate task force's meeting last month, the WNBA said conversations will continue. "We will continue to engage all league stakeholders in the coming weeks and months," the statement read in part. "We will approach these important conversations thoughtfully and in alignment with the values of our league."

A major factor for the WNBA is the commissioner. Engelbert announced on Sept. 4 that she plans to depart her role at the end of 2026. Her replacement will be an important voice in the discussion.

That likely makes any substantive policy change a long way off.

The union, when asked by ESPN, declined to comment on its stance on Kanter Freedom and White's eligibility. Some players, including Cloud, Stefanie Dolson and union executive committee member Brianna Turner, have shown support for transgender inclusion broadly. Most have remained silent. Cunningham, when asked last week by ESPN, did not endorse the NBA players' eligibility claims.

"I'm gonna let them do them," she said.

stories.headline: Azerbaijan Grand Prix 2026: Race start time in Baku, how to watch, full schedule, predictions
stories.summary: Formula 1 is heading to the streets of Baku for this year's Azerbaijan Grand Prix as we roll into the business end of the season.
stories.body:
Formula 1 is heading to the streets of Baku for this year's Azerbaijan Grand Prix as we roll into the business end of the season.

Title leader Kimi Antonelli extended his lead in the drivers' championship after picking up his eighth victory of the season at the brand-new Madring last time out.

He leads his teammate George Russell by 81 points, with Lewis Hamilton now dropping back in the title race after a retirement in Spain.

So you don't miss a thing, here's everything you need to know for the 15th race of the season.

- Madring's F1 debut left everyone dissatisfied, even Spanish GP's top 3

- Max Verstappen wins Max vs 100 in style after overtaking 100 go-karters in 35 minutes

- F1 2027 calendar: Monaco GP gets sprint race, Türkiye and Portugal return to schedule

Azerbaijan Grand Prix schedule
All times in BST

Thursday, September 24

Practice One: 9.30 a.m. - 10.30 a.m.

Practice Two: 1 p.m. - 2 p.m.

Friday, September 25

Final Practice: 9.30 a.m. - 10.30 a.m.

Qualifying: 1 p.m. - 2 p.m.

Saturday, September 26

Azerbaijan Grand Prix: 12 p.m.

How to watch

Sky Sports has exclusive F1 rights again in 2026 in the U.K., with every session live on Sky Sports F1. The sessions are also on Sky Sports Main Event.

For non-subscribers, highlights of the Azerbaijan Grand Prix will be on free-to-air television on Channel 4.

In the U.S., subscribers can watch every session on Apple TV, via a new F1 channel on the platform.

Why is the race on a Saturday?
For the first time in Baku's history, the F1 weekend will shift a day forwards, with the race taking place on a Saturday to avoid a clash with an Azerbaijan National Day of mourning on the Sunday.

Azerbaijan's people will dedicate their thoughts to military personnel and those who died during the Second Nagorno-Karabakh War.

Baku City Circuit

After the European leg of the calendar where circuits are more traditional, Baku is one of the standout street circuits of the season.

The first race in Baku was held in 2016 as the European Grand Prix before it was called the Azerbaijan Grand Prix a year later.

The section around Turns 8, 9 and 10 are lined by the walls of the city's charming old town including a castle and the long main straight along the Baku shoreline sees cars reach speeds in excess of 220 mph and is the best spot for overtaking.

The walls are narrow and the high-speeds make for either a race full of chaos, or none at all. There is a 57% chance of a Safety Car being deployed during the race.

Azerbaijan Grand Prix

Circuit: Baku City Circuit; Baku, Azerbaijan

Previous winners
2016: Nico Rosberg (Mercedes)

2017: Daniel Ricciardo (Red Bull)

2018: Lewis Hamilton (Mercedes)

2019: Valtteri Bottas (Mercedes)

2021: Sergio Pérez (Red Bull)

2022: Max Verstappen (Red Bull)

2023: Sergio Pérez (Red Bull)

2024: Oscar Piastri (McLaren)

2025: Max Verstappen (Red Bull)

Other key stats

First F1 race: 2016 European GP. (First race as Azerbaijan GP in 2017)

Laps: 51 laps of 6km.

Lap record: 1:43.009, Charles Leclerc (2019).

Most wins: Pérez (2021, 2023) and Verstappen (2022, 2025) with two wins each. Other winners from the current grid are Hamilton (2018), Bottas (2019) and Piastri (2024).

Most poles: Leclerc with four (2021-2024) and Hamilton (2017), Bottas (2019) and Verstappen (2025) are the other pole sitters from the current grid.

Weather forecast

The weather for the Azerbaijan Grand Prix will be dry and sunny throughout the weekend. Temperatures will be around 26°C, but will drop to 24°C for the race on Saturday.

What happened last year?
Red Bull's Verstappen took pole position around the streets of Baku in a qualifying session that featured a record six red flags.

He ended up converting that pole into a dominant victory, with Russell in second and Carlos Sainz behind.

It was a key moment in the championship fight between Lando Norris and Piastri as Norris closed the gap to 25 points to his McLaren teammate after the Australian crashed out.

Who will win this year?

The last street circuit this year was in Monaco in June and since then several of the top teams have upgraded its packages and haven't yet gone racing on street circuits, but Baku has now arrived.

Antonelli has looked on fire in the last two races, but Norris is creeping to the front. The reigning world champion has two wins to his name in Hungary and Zandvoort, but also suffered an unlucky run in Madrid with the safety car deployment, so missed out on a potential win there as well.

Mercedes are set to be quick in the high-speed straight lines in Baku, but the tight and twisty corners might suit Ferrari and McLaren best.

One of the main aims will be to not crash the car into the wall otherwise the whole course of the race can rapidly change in a blink of an eye.

stories.headline: Still at zero: Viral Man United fan's haircut challenge nears two years
stories.summary: Viral Manchester United fan Frank Ilett's haircut challenge is nearing the two-year mark and he's back to square 1.
stories.body:
For most clubs, failure or success can be defined in points, trophies and medals. Manchester United are the same, but they can also define it in days. More specifically, it can be summed up in 712 days.

That's how long viral United fan Frank Ilett, also known as The United Strand, has gone without a haircut as he waits for the team to win five games in a row.

After finishing last season with wins over Nottingham Forest and Brighton, Michael Carrick's side could have completed the job with wins over newly promoted Hull City and Ipswich Town before finishing with a win away at Everton. As it turned out, that's not at all what happened.

An embarrassing 2-0 away defeat to Hull meant going back to square one. A 5-2 win over Ipswich might have promoted hopes that the season opener was just an unwanted blip, but a draw to Everton and a controversial defeat to 10-man Manchester City poured further cold water.

How could it get worse? Well, a 2-0 lead inside the first 10 minutes against Brighton in the Carabao Cup ended in a surprise 3-2 defeat.

Left watching on, his hair growing ever longer, is Ilett. His challenge will now officially reach the two-year mark -- his last haircut was on Oct. 5, 2024 -- and his hair is now almost 14 inches at its longest point.

In the meantime, Ilett continues to raise money for the Little Princess Trust, which creates wigs for children with cancer.

The only thing that can happen now before Ilett soars past two years is for United to win away to Fulham in their last game before the international break.

stories.headline: Roosters' make call on star forward, Walker progress
stories.summary: Angus Crichton has been cleared to return for the Roosters in their knockout clash with Cronulla, with star halfback Sam Walker not too far behind him.
stories.body:
Test forward Angus Crichton is set to turbo-charge the Sydney Roosters' forward pack as Trent Robinson confirmed the back-rower had received the green light to take on Cronulla.

Crichton, who will move to rugby union whenever the Roosters' season ends, hasn't played since round 15 as a result of a foot injury.

The 30-year-old was a late scratching in last week's qualifying final loss to Penrith.

But Robinson, who provided a glimmer of hope surrounding the fitness of halfback Sam Walker, confirmed 17-time State of Origin star Crichton had been cleared to face the Sharks in Saturday's semi-final at Allianz Stadium.

"(He's) ready to go," Robinson said on Friday.

"I don't think the standard of the game changes when it comes to Angus.

"He'll get on the field but he has played enough of these sort of quality games to get ready to go back in.

"He wasn't ready to go last week, that was the truth of it. He still had some issues last week and he hasn't had them this week, so ready to go."

Young tyro Salesi Foketi would likely make way for Crichton if Robinson chooses to start his experienced edge forward.

"He could start or come off the bench. Gus is ready to go, he'll be in the mix. He's going to hunt," Robinson said.

Victory against the Sharks would send the Roosters into a preliminary final against the Dolphins and Robinson is hopeful Walker will be ready to feature, should his side get past a Cronulla team led by his former protege Craig Fitzgibbon.

Walker underwent ankle surgery three weeks ago but has been back running in a positive sign for Easts' hopes of winning the premiership.

"It's good (Walker had) another good progression this week," Robinson said.

"(He needs to) keep going. There's a little bit less weight on that ankle compared to other guys in our game, so he's progressing well.

"He's a chance (to play next week).

"Most of those guys end up doing running, straight line running, and all of that, whereas he's back into some free movement and into some training, so that's a real positive."

Robinson's side enter Saturday's meeting with Cronulla off a six-day turnaround from the Penrith game and they face the same shortened period of rest if they get past the Sharks to face the Dolphins.

The NRL's finals draw has been complicated by the Warriors making the top four and the flow-on effect of scheduling games at times which suit both Australian and New Zealand broadcasters.

By contrast Newcastle, who face the Warriors on Sunday, will be given a nine-day break between their week-one finals win over Souths.

But Robinson refused to call foul over his side's shortened lead-in to the most important games of the Roosters' season.

"I think we'll do whatever it takes to play finals," Robinson said. "That's as simple as it is.

"I think it's a real fair question around how it's scheduled and why we schedule them in this way, but they're the cards we're dealt and we're ready to play on six days, five days, four days, whatever it takes."

stories.headline: Nats reward ace Cade Cavalli with 4-year contract through 2030
stories.summary: Pitcher Cade Cavalli and the Washington Nationals have agreed to a four-year contract through the 2030 season, a deal that includes a team option for 2031.
stories.body:
WASHINGTON -- Pitcher Cade Cavalli and the Washington Nationals agreed Friday to a four-year contract through the 2030 season, a deal that includes a team option for 2031.

Cavalli and the team agreed in January to a one-year contract with $862,500 guaranteed: an $862,500 salary this year and a $4 million team option for 2027 with a $7,500 buyout. He would have been eligible for free agency after the 2029 season.

"We've seen firsthand the work he's put in, the challenges he's overcome and the way he continues to grow as a pitcher, a person and a leader," president of baseball operations Paul Toboni said in a statement. "Our organization has tremendous belief in Cade, and, more importantly, we're incredibly proud to have him represent the Washington Nationals for years to come. We're so excited to watch the next chapter of his career unfold here with us."

Cavalli, who turned 28 on Aug. 14, is 12-5 with a 3.12 ERA this season and is tied for ninth in the major leagues with 194 strikeouts. He has allowed three earned runs or fewer in 29 of his 31 starts this season, the most in baseball.

Washington selected him with the 22nd pick in the 2020 amateur draft. He debuted in 2022, then was injured the following spring training and had Tommy John reconstructive elbow surgery that caused him to miss all of 2023 and most of 2024.

Cavalli made it back to the Nationals by August of last year and this season was their Opening Day starter.

"Since we drafted Cade in 2020, we've been continually impressed with who he is as a baseball player and as a human being," owner Mark Lerner said. "He's shown that he not only has the talent to excel as a major leaguer, but he also possesses the high character and leadership qualities that make him a beloved member of our clubhouse and in the community."

stories.headline: Bills to take time with Ed Oliver, DJ Moore injuries
stories.summary: A long week will give more time for Bills defensive lineman Ed Oliver (hip) and wide receiver DJ Moore (shoulder) to get healthy following Thursday's injuries.
stories.body:
Call it a not-so-mad scramble.

The Buffalo Bills lost defensive lineman Ed Oliver and wide receiver DJ Moore to injury before and during their 41-31 win over the Detroit Lions on Thursday night. As coach Joe Brady told reporters Friday, the team will slow-play the evaluation process with both Oliver and Moore.

The Bills don't return to the practice field until Sept. 23, and as such Brady said he's holding off on rushing judgments or prognoses on the two starters until the team can see what rest does for them.

Moore is considered day-to-day with a shoulder injury sustained in the second quarter of the win over Detroit that's not considered serious, sources told ESPN's Adam Schefter.

Oliver, meanwhile, didn't play against Detroit. He sustained the hip injury just minutes before the pregame deadline for players to be ruled inactive. Brady said Friday that Oliver was in the training room getting evaluated about three minutes before the deadline came, which forced the Bills to make a quick choice about one of their cornerstone defensive linemen.

"If it was normal maybe you'd have an hour or so to run some tests and see what happens," Brady said. "We didn't have that time. We just had to make the decisions."

Bills defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard described Oliver -- who has logged 30 sacks and 57 tackles for loss across eight seasons in Buffalo but missed 14 games last year with injuries -- as a player you build a game plan around. Removing his presence from the game plan barely an hour before kickoff creates a scramble, but not one Leonhard would describe as "frantic."

Leonhard said the minutes following Oliver's deactivation consisted of meetings with defensive position coaches to strategize not just who would replace Oliver in certain packages but also conversations about what the domino effect in the rotations would be and which packages needed to be eliminated entirely.

"It's not necessarily just one chess piece away," Leonhard said. "It's a couple moves away that we'd have some deviations. Just trying to go through all the scenarios of what can happen and make sure all the depth and the rotations are going to be in a situation to allow you to play 45 snaps or 85 snaps. That's the uncertainty; you never know how the game is going to play out."

The Bills return to action in Week 3 with a home game against the Los Angeles Chargers on Sept. 27.

stories.headline: Transfer rumors, news: Real Madrid, Barcelona track Man City-bound USMNT star Sullivan
stories.summary: Real Madrid and Barcelona could make a future move for USMNT youngster Cavan Sullivan. Transfer Talk has the latest.
stories.body:
Real Madrid and Barcelona could make a future move for USMNT teenager Cavan Sullivan, after his move to Manchester City in 2028, while Arsenal are interested in a move for AFC Bournemouth forward Junior Kroupi in January. Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Real Madrid and Barcelona could make a future move for USMNT youngster Cavan Sullivan, 16, according to TEAMtalk. The midfielder has impressed since making his breakthrough in MLS as a 14-year-old and has cemented his place in the senior team at Philadelphia Union this season, with six goals and five assists in 23 league appearances. That form has earned him a place in Mauricio Pochettino's most-recent USMNT squad. Sullivan has already agreed to join Manchester City when he turns 18, but the report claims Spain's top two are keeping a close eye on his development and could swoop if he doesn't make the breakthrough into their first XI quickly.

- Arsenal are interested in a move for AFC Bournemouth forward Junior Kroupi in January once he has recovered from injury, says Football.London. Kroupi, 20, scored 13 goals in 35 games last season as the Cherries sealed European football for the first time, but the club would consider offers of over £80 million to let him go. Arsenal already have Kai Havertz and Viktor Gyökeres up front but are looking to strengthen across their forward line after the exits of Gabriel Jesus, Gabriel Martinelli and Leandro Trossard.

- Bayern Munich are considering a move for Benfica center back Tomás Araújo, according to Tuttomercatoweb. Araújo, 24, is reported to be available for around €40 million but his arrival is reported to be tied to that of Kim Min-Jae and, according to Bild's Christian Falk, Bayern are planning fresh talks with the South Korea international over a new contract. The 29-year-old only has two years left on his deal, which runs until 2028, sparking the discussions about his future. The report claims that it comes as something of a surprise, as Bayern were open to an exit over the summer if the right offer arrived.

- Everton are open to accepting a loan exit for winger Tyler Dibling in the January transfer window, claims Football Insider. The 20-year-old has struggled to assert himself in David Moyes' immediate plans, having failed to make a Premier League appearance so far this season. Development is still the priority for the youngster, whose transfer from Southampton cost £40 million in 2025, and the January window offers an opportunity for Everton to strengthen an already depleted squad before letting him go.

- FC Cincinnati have reached an agreement to sign former Manchester United defender Tyrell Malacia, according to Voetbal International. The left back, who left Old Trafford as a free agent this summer, has reportedly been training with the MLS outfit with the hopes of landing a deal. Now an agreement has been reached, with the report claiming that a deal until mid-2027 has been outlined, with an option to extend by another year. The 27-year-old turned down options in LaLiga and Brazil.

Other rumors
- Chelsea have no plans to allow Estevao to leave the club following reports linking the Brazilian with a £100 million move to Liverpool. (TEAMtalk)

- Liverpool are working on a January deal for AS Monaco midfielder Lamine Camara after opening preliminary talks with his representatives. (Football Insider)

- Liverpool will consider allowing midfielder Wataru Endo to leave in January as he enters the final six months of his contract. (GMS)

- Newcastle United manager Matthias Jaissle will make a final decision on a contract extension for defender Dan Burn, whose current deal expires next summer. (Football Insider)

- Aston Villa have downplayed concerns surrounding the future of Alejandro Garnacho, as doubts have emerged over the winger's permanent move to the club next summer. (TEAMtalk)

- Barcelona are monitoring Espanyol forward Roberto Fernandez alongside interest from Hull City, Como, and Fiorentina. (Ekrem Konur)

- Barcelona are in advanced talks with forward Raphinha over a new contract extension, with his current deal expiring in 2028. (Marca)

- Manchester City and Atletico Madrid have made contact over a move for Bayer Leverkusen playmaker Ibrahim Maza, who is also being tracked by Arsenal and Manchester United. (Ekrem Konur)

- Leeds United are in no rush to trigger their €23 million option to permanently sign on-loan Eintracht Frankfurt forward Jean-Matteo Bahoya. (AS)

stories.headline: Brentford 3-0 Chelsea: Premier League action as Bees sink Xabi Alonso's Blues - as it happened
stories.summary: Goals from Jaidon Anthony, Igor Thiago and Fábio Carvalho see Brentford beat Chelsea. Follow reaction with ESPN.
stories.body:
Brentford earned their first ever win over Chelsea in the Premier League on Friday after a 3-0 victory at the GTech.

The hosts move up to third in the table ahead of the rest of the weekend's fixtures and remain unbeaten in the Premier League this season.

It was a puzzling display for Xabi Alonso to ponder after watching his team impose themselves on the hosts in the first half yet struggling to find a goal threat, before succumbing in the second period to goals from Jaidon Anthony, Igor Thiago and Fábio Carvalho.

- Xabi Alonso thanks Todd Boehly, Mark Walter after Chelsea sale

- João Pedro withdraws from Brazil squad with injury

It's been another eventful week behind the scenes at Chelsea with the news that co-owners Todd Boehly and Mark Walter have sold their stakes in the club.

Boehly and Walter have sold their stakes in Chelsea -- having each owned 12.83% -- to give Clearlake Capital -- which previously held 61.5% -- full control of the London club.

The consortium bought Chelsea in 2022 for £2.5 billion ($3.3 billion), with a further £1.75 billion ($2.3 billion) committed to investment. The club's sale came after former owner Roman Abramovich was sanctioned by alleged ties to Russia president Vladimir Putin following the country's invasion of Ukraine.

Swiss philanthropist Hansjörg Wyss, who also owned a 12.83% stake, will remain a partner in the ownership group, the club has confirmed.

Chelsea manager Alonso said it was time to "move on together."

"I think it is an important day for the club when there is an important change in the structure of the club, new ownership," Alonso told a news conference on Thursday.

"Thanks to the former owners for what they have done. I was not here but I know that they played an important role. And now that Behdad [Eghbali] is taking more control, or almost full control, I think it is good that the main one is clear."

stories.headline: Fantasy hockey sleepers and busts: Players to draft or avoid at current draft spot
stories.summary: Who are the players going too high, or too low, compared to their expected fantasy hockey production?
stories.body:
Overachievers. In fantasy competition, to identify and secure them is to love them. There's no better complement to our unsurprising stars and other reliable contributors than a player (or more) who blows our too-modest preseason expectations right out of the rink. Whether of the breakout, bounce-back, or other variety, sleepers -- grabbed in late stages of a draft or even once play is underway -- go a long way in helping any competitive manager contend for a championship.

For this exercise, we're focusing on skaters who have been around the block a bit, as opposed to rookies or other breakout candidates like Jimmy Snuggerud, Jackson Blake, and Will Smith. We're tackling those similarly coveted fantasy performers elsewhere in our department. Also, you might notice a trend of fresh faces in new places applying to many of the following sleeper candidates. That's no coincidence. These potentially underrated fantasy skaters were not only actively pursued by their new teams, but acquired to fill a prominent position, which offers them an improved opportunity to make a bigger splash than otherwise.

Of course, you also want to avoid using too high of a draft pick in selecting players belonging on the other end of the meeting-expectations spectrum. So we're also including a few possible busts to steer clear of overly early on.

Sleepers

Patrick Kane, F, Chicago Blackhawks (RW30)

They don't call him "Showtime" for nothing. Mark it, the 37-year-old is going to put on a sparkling display in his return to Chicago. If healthy enough, Kane's going to produce. It's as simple as that. The future Hall-of-Famer hasn't averaged more than a point/game for his 19-year career by happenstance. As for the winger's current physical condition, according to the Chicago Sun-Times, head coach Jeff Blashill believes his veteran star is feeling fit.

"He feels as good as he has in a long time. He's skating well, he's moving well," Blashill said. "Guys that play with their brain first seem to last a long time in this league, and he certainly has."

Then consider the eventual top-line and power-play assignment alongside burgeoning superstar Connor Bedard, who's due to return from a shoulder injury in early November. (Kane will make do well enough with gifted rookie center Anton Frondell or whoever else in the meanwhile.) All promising stuff. If the vet can carve out upwards of 70 games this campaign, he's well worth rostering in most leagues.

Mats Zuccarello, F, Los Angeles Kings (RW36)

Sure, he'll miss playing with winger Kirill Kaprizov in Minnesota. Who wouldn't? But there are much worse fates than landing on a top unit and power play with Artemi Panarin. Perennially underrated as a fantasy asset, all Zuccarello does is produce regularly. Averaging 0.92 points/game this past season, the 39-year-old is hardly slowing down with age. Durability remains the only concern here, as the veteran hasn't banged out anything near a complete season since 2022-23. But that's why you have IR spots. Draft Zuccarello late as a potential gem in his new Los Angeles digs.

Valeri Nichushkin, F, Columbus Blue Jackets (LW24)

When healthy and active -- admittedly an issue over the years in Dallas and Colorado -- the power forward is capable of putting up fantasy numbers with the best of them. He shoots, hits, scores and contributes frequently on the power play. After a modest year by his standards, the ex-Avalanche is now set to enjoy a fresh start as a more prominent player in Columbus. No longer in the company of Nathan MacKinnon, Martin Necas, Gabriel Landeskog and others, Nichushkin can sink his teeth into a larger role on a top line and power play with Jackets star and countryman Kirill Marchenko. The 31-year-old played 72 contests this past regular season, more than he has in a long while. At his best, Nichushkin is capable of averaging 2.0 points/game in ESPN standard leagues.

Gabriel Landeskog, F, Colorado Avalanche (N/A)

Ranking-wise, MacKinnon is cream of the fantasy crop in ESPN standard competition. Reasonably enough, Necas sits several notches below at 31st overall. Then we need to scroll all the way down to realize Landeskog isn't even included in the top 250. Bit odd, considering the Avalanche captain is slated to play with the aforementioned pair on Colorado's top line and power play. Or that he collected 11 points in 13 playoff games after his first full-ish season following what essentially amounted to a three-year absence from the game. Healthy and fit, which he is now, the still-only 33-year-old is capable of putting up 70 points alongside MacKinnon and Necas. No question, he's worth grabbing in deeper leagues.

Mason Marchment, F, San Jose Sharks (N/A)

After showing flashes of potential in Florida and Dallas and Seattle and Columbus, the too-well traveled veteran now gets to play with Macklin Celebrini in San Jose. If he manages to keep a grip on that assignment, the 31-year-old is going to score 30 goals and 35-plus assists this season. A gig on San Jose's top power play, again alongside Celebrini, isn't out of the question either.

Jiri Kulich, F, Buffalo Sabres (N/A)

More specifically qualifying as a breakout candidate, Kulich still very comfortably fits the broader "sleeper" mold heading into 2026-27. After suffering a devastating -- and potentially career-ending -- blood clot last November, the 22-year-old underwent successful surgery and is ready to resume play. Selected 28th overall in 2022, he's expected to be offered the ripe opportunity to make a profound impression on a top line with Tage Thompson and fellow breakout candidate Zach Benson. If that's how it indeed shakes out in Buffalo, draft Kulich late in deeper leagues or off the wire before regular play gets underway. Before your fellow managers become more familiar with the kid who scored 15 goals in 62 games as a rookie two years ago.

Adam Fox, D, New York Rangers (D27)

D27? So we should draft 26 other NHL defenders before the guy who won the Norris five years ago? Who, at 28 years old, still enjoys top-pair minutes and competes on New York's No. 1 power play? That guy? I get that Fox may have fallen off some fantasy radars after losing a chunk of time to injury last season, but he still collected 53 points, including 24 with the extra skater, in 55 games. And the top-15 fantasy defenseman is once again healthy.

Stuart Skinner, G, Winnipeg Jets (G32)

So now camp no-show Connor Hellebuyck is suspended by the Jets. Hmm. Does this action further inspire management and hasten the goalie's exit out of Winnipeg, or do matters become even messier? Regardless, Skinner remains in place and is revving to go. The recent two-time Stanley Cup Finalist is presently the undisputed No. 1 for a solid-enough Jets team that's ready to put last year's debacle behind it. While this situation remains fluid -- GM Kevin Cheveldayoff could/should acquire a quality netminder as part of a package in return for Hellebuyck -- Skinner is still worth a flyer in all but the shallowest of fantasy leagues.

Seth Jones, D, Florida Panthers (N/A)
Jacob Markstrom , G, Florida Panthers (G30)

Made it this far? Create your own league with your own rules and play against your friends today.

Busts

Steven Stamkos, F, Nashville Predators (C14)

He isn't likely to score 40-plus again this season. According to Evolving Hockey, Stamkos should have netted approximately 34 goals (34.33 ixG) in 2025-26, not 42. His unsustainable 20.4% shooting percentage supports such evaluation. Projected to average around 17 minutes/game on Nashville's second line and the top power play, Stamkos sports a realistic ceiling of 30-35 goals and 25 assists, with a solid number of points counting with the man-advantage. Decent numbers indeed, but not near top-30. There are about 25 other NHL forwards who I would draft before the 36-year-old veteran.

Alex Ovechkin, F, Washington Capitals (LW11)

It's all relative, right? As a fantasy performer, this isn't your mother's Ovechkin. At 41 years old, the greatest goal-scorer of all time is back for another kick at the Stanley Cup can. If contributions from supporting castmates, including a host of newbies like Alex Tuch, Jordan Kyrou and Boone Jenner, help him get there, personal stats be darned. Sure, he'll flirt with 30 goals on a pile of shots in a full, healthy season (tougher ask this round with no elongated Olympic break), and many of them will count on the power play. But, again, there are too many other options around the league with greater fantasy potential. Especially if Ovechkin drops down the Caps lineup, as anticipated.

Morgan Geekie, F, Boston Bruins (C34)

Receiving positive attention in this space as a sleeper candidate last season, the Bruins winger didn't disappoint those willing to take the early plunge. At least until Christmas. Less notably, after scoring 25 goals in his first 36 games, Geekie only managed another 14 in his final 45. Which leaves us less optimistic about the 28-year-old's prospects this campaign, even if he remains on David Pastrnak's wing.

Brent Burns, D, Colorado Avalanche (D45)

Unless your preferred team is facing him in the Final, who wouldn't want to see Burns hoist the Stanley Cup? We all love the 41-year-old defender. But his finest fantasy days are behind him. Pegged to play on the third pair in Colorado and unlikely to enjoy any significant time with the extra skater, Burns projects to put up 30 or so even-strength points and not enough blocked shots to compensate otherwise. According to Evolving Hockey, he was supposed to score only six goals (6.62 ixG), yet he potted 12. The fourth-ranked fantasy defender on his own team behind Cale Makar, Devon Toews and Sam Malinski, Burns should only be rostered in deeper ESPN conventional leagues. His durability isn't enough.

Dan Vladar, G, Philadelphia Flyers (G18)

Joseph Woll is a good goalie. Better than Samuel Ersson. If the former Maple Leaf remains healthy, he'll eat into Vladar's playing time. Then there's the incumbent's small sample size. As impressed as we all are with how the ex-Flame conducted himself in his first year as Philly's go-to, it was just the one season. Plus, are the Flyers a playoff team again? In the Metropolitan Division, the Capitals are better, no one would be surprised to see the Devils and Rangers improve on their respective records, and Carolina remains Carolina. There's another crowd of netminders I'm chasing before Vladar as my second fantasy goalie in deeper leagues.
